 Dated this the 09th day of July 2025
 Judgment

These appeals under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) have been filed by the third respondent/insurer in O.P.(MV) Nos.377/2017 and 376/2017 respectively on the file of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Thodupuzha (the Tribunal) aggrieved by the Award dated 27/07/2019.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents in MACA Nos.191/2020 and 435/2020 are the claim petitioners and respondents 1 & 2 respectively in the original petition.

In these appeals, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.
2. According to the claim petitioners, on 16/11/2016 at about 08:30 p.m., while the petitioners were travelling in an autorickshaw bearing registration No.KL 38F 2415 through M.A.C.A.Nos.191 & 435 of 2020 2025:KER:50492 Pattayakudi-Venmani pubilc road and when they reached the place by name Venmani bhagam, due to the rash and negligent driving of the 1st respondent/driver, the vehicle rammed the side wall of the road and overturned as a result of which they sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent/driver and the second respondent/owner filed written statements admitting the existence of a valid policy for the offending vehicle.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy.

The age, income,
nature of injuries sustained etc. were disputed.
It was also contended that the amount claimed was excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A13 were marked on the side of the claim petitioners.
Exts.B1 to B3 were marked on the side of the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found M.A.C.A.Nos.191 & 435 of 2020 2025:KER:50492 negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the autorickshaw resulting in the incident and hence awarded amounts of 5,98,157/- and 5,01,719/- respectively together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realisation with proportionate costs in MACA Nos.191/2020 and 435/2020 respectively.
Aggrieved by the Award, the third respondent/insurer has come up in appeals.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in these appeals is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.

9. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the first respondent/driver did not have a license for driving commercial vehicles and therefore, there is a New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Sanumon.T.H on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150991832/
4 violation of the policy conditions and hence the third respondent/insurer cannot be held liable for the award amount.
9.1.

sentences.text: 10. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following head is challenged by the third respondent/insurer - Pain and suffering 10.1.

It was submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the amount of compensation awarded under this head for both the claim petitioners is on the higher side and hence, the same needs to be reduced appropriately.

11. The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries:-
"frontal extra dural haemorrhage, contused abrasion forehead and contusion right foot dorsum."
Ext.A10 discharge summary shows that there was right frontal bone fracture and that he underwent surgery right frontal craniotomy and evacuation of EDH.

In the light of the nature of the injuries sustained by him and the surgery he had to undergo, I find that the M.A.C.A.Nos.191 & 435 of 2020 2025:KER:50492 amount of 1,00,000/- that has been granted by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering is just and reasonable.

12. The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries:-
"undisplaced fracture of transverse process of L2, L3 and L4 vertebrae, contused abrasion right elbow and contusion left knee."
An amount of 1,00,000/- was claimed.

In the light of the injuries sustained by the claim petitioner,
I find that an amount of 75,000/- towards pain and suffering would be just and reasonable.
